subject: ACME: VPC Performance SLO follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: VPC performance targets (recap + items)

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — useful conversation. Quick recap of the performance constraints you shared and next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of ACME targets (as discussed):
- 95th pct latency target (in-region): <= 200ms end-to-end for streamed chat prompts (including client-to-service network hops).
- Median latency target: <= 80ms for non-streaming generation.
- Concurrency: sustained 500 concurrent streamed sessions with bursts to 1,500 for peak events.
- Throughput: baseline 20 tokens/sec per stream average; expected aggregate ~10M tokens/day.
- Streaming requirements: server-side chunking + immediate flush to client (no 200ms batching).

Private/VPC specifics we noted:
- Connectivity: you prefer VPC peering over VPN; fallback to IPsec VPN if peering not possible.
- Egress: traffic to Redwood endpoints will require controlled egress paths; you requested egress cost estimate and whether we can accept private peering to avoid NAT egress.
- Internal latency budget: ACME internal appl -> edge hop should be <= 30ms to meet E2E targets.
- MTU, path MTU discovery, and TLS handshake times may matter for streaming small frames — flagged for network ops.

Action items / owners:
1) Marissa (me) — send SLO checklist + attach network diagram to confirm topology assumptions (attached).
2) Sam / Network Ops — share traceroutes and ping samples from app hosts to our proposed peering CIDR; indicate whether Direct Connect / Cloud Interconnect is used.
3) Aditya (cc'd) — run quick model-level latency profile to estimate token latency contribution for the model variant we discussed (openquant-13B).
4) Priya — indicate any procurement timelines or compliance checkpoints that would affect Dedicated or Private deployment.

If any of the targets above are off, correct me and I’ll update. Next meeting suggestion: 30-min technical sync with your netops and our infra team Wednesday 2026-04-22 10:00 PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network_diagram.pdf (application/pdf, 140KB)]

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, Network Ops <netops@acme.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC performance targets (recap + items)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. Confirming the recap is accurate. A couple clarifications: 

- 95th pct target is for user-visible token emission latency; we need <200ms E2E for the interactive assistant flows.
- For peering: we prefer VPC peering but requires approval from infra; netops will validate route table/overlap.
- We will provide traceroutes, and also a sample of 10k pings from our app frontends to your proposed egress IPs.
- Procurement timeline: aiming to have a POC contract signed by end of May if netops and SLOs validate.

I can confirm Wed 4/22 at 10:00 PT for the technical sync — adding it to calendars.

Sam
Director, Product Engineering
Acme Robotics

On top of traceroutes, netops will want to know: expected connection type (AWS Transit Gateway / VPC Peer / GCP VPC peering), whether we require BGP, and any recommended CIDR subnets for peering.

From: Network Ops <netops@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC performance targets (recap + items)

Marissa,

Looping in NetOps. We captured a few follow-ups after an internal review:
- Please provide recommended peering CIDR ranges and the preferred cloud interconnect (we are on AWS in us-west-2 and GCP in us-east1 for DR).
- Will Redwood accept a private peering enum with static routes, or do you require AWS TGW with route propagation and BGP?
- For streaming, we need guidance on how persistent TCP/TLS connections should be handled (idle timeout, keepalive).
- Please confirm whether egress will be charged back to ACME if using public egress IPs versus a private peering link.

We will attach traceroute logs in a separate email but are starting with single-region validation.

Thanks,
Alex (NetOps)
Acme Robotics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Network Ops <netops@acme.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC performance targets (recap + items)

Alex — thanks for the list. Covering each item below and attaching our SLO checklist workbook so you can fill in what you can from your side: 

- Recommended CIDR / peering: we can support either VPC peering or TGW/interconnect. Recommended: a /24 per region to avoid overlap; if you prefer TGW with BGP we can accept route propagation — BGP is optional but helpful for failover.
- Static routes vs BGP: static peering is supported; we typically recommend BGP for resiliency but will work with static routes for POC.
- TCP/TLS handling: keepalive every 30s, idle timeout 300s for persistent streams. We recommend configuring NAT / idle TCP timeout to >6 minutes to avoid premature closes during long-running sessions.
- Egress billing: if traffic goes over public internet egress IPs, egress will be metered to ACME; private peering can be arranged to avoid public egress costs — we'll provide an estimated delta after you share expected traffic volumes.

Aditya will run the model-level latency profile and share a short table with token-level latency contributions. Monica from Solutions will own the SOW/procurement check questions.

I'll bring these into the tech sync on Wed. Attached: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (fill columns marked "ACME input").

Best,
Marissa

[Attachment: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 36KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Network Ops <netops@acme.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC performance targets (recap + items)

Quick note from the infra/model side after a quick run:
- Model variant openquant-13B (configured at 8-bit quant) adds ~35-45ms per token at median on an rtx A100 class env; 95th percentile token contribution ~85ms in our test harness (single-token generation path).
- For streamed workloads, network + TLS + client flush cost will add ~40-120ms depending on path; so your 200ms 95th E2E target is tight but feasible with private peering and optimized client-side flush behavior.
- Scaling: to support sustained 500 concurrent streams we recommend a dedicated pool with autoscale headroom; we'll propose instance counts in the tech sync.

I'll prepare a quick slide with a recommended instance mix and an estimated latency breakdown (model / runtime / network).

— Aditya
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
